 ```
 
 For each line `<N> <login> <time>`:
-- **withdrawn** - `<login>` commented `unclaim` (or `/unclaim`) after
-  `<time>`: skip silently. A withdrawn claim's old comment is never
-  mirrored again (without this the Withdraw pass and this one would flip
-  the label every run);
+- **ended** - after `<time>`, `<login>` withdrew the claim in a later
+  comment (`unclaim`, `/unclaim`, "claim withdrawn", "releasing this
+  claim", "the issue is free"), or a comment says the claim was "released
+  by the maintainer" or "released (stale ...)": skip silently. An ended
+  claim's old comment is never mirrored again, whatever the claimant
+  comments afterwards - only a NEW `claimed:` / `/claim` line is a claim
+  (without this the Withdraw pass and this one would flip the label every
+  run);
 - **paused issue** (labelled `P?` - AGENTS.md "`P?` is paused"): do not
   mirror; reply once (only if no later comment mentions `@<login>`)
   `This issue is paused by the maintainer (P?) - it isn't open for work yet; the claim isn't recorded. It will be once the maintainer sets a priority.`;
 - **closed issue**, or **already mirrored** (`claimed` set and `<login>`
   assigned, or `claimed` set and a "Claim recorded for @<login>" reply
   exists): skip silently;
-- **held by someone else** - an earlier claim comment by another
-  contributor still exists, or a fresh agent claim (4 h rule): do not
+- **held by someone else** - an earlier claim by another contributor is
+  still LIVE (not ended, and it passes the liveness test below), or one of
+  the owner account's agents holds a fresh claim (4 h rule): do not
   mirror; reply once (only if no later comment mentions `@<login>`) naming
-  the current claimant;
+  the current claimant. A stale or ended earlier claim holds nothing: if
+  the earlier one is stale and not yet released, release it NOW (remove
+  that claimant's assignment and post the stale-release comment from the
+  Withdraw pass - it ends that claim), then judge this claim on its own
+  merits. The label and the assignee always follow the newest live claim,
+  and the Withdraw pass judges the claim of the current assignee;
+- **stale** (AGENTS.md "A claim must be live"): the claim is not live -
+  no open PR by the claimant for the issue, no commit on the claimant's
+  branch for it in the last 48 hours, and no comment by the claimant on
+  the issue in the last 48 hours (a comment that withdraws or releases
+  the claim is not activity: ended beats live). Do not mirror; skip
+  silently. Check
+  liveness with
+  `gh pr list --state open --author "<login>" --search "<N> in:title,body" --json number,headRefName`
+  (then confirm the PR really is for this issue: its body or branch names
+  `<N>`), the dates of `<login>`'s comments on the issue, and, for a
+  branch the claim names,
+  `gh api "repos/<login>/Camcraft/commits?sha=<branch>&per_page=1" --jq '.[0].commit.committer.date'`
+  (the branch lives in the claimant's fork, so the owner in the path is
+  the claimant's login; if the call errors - no such fork or branch -
+  count it as no recent commit);
 - **otherwise**: `gh issue edit N --add-label claimed --add-assignee <login>`
   (if GitHub refuses the assignee, add the label alone) and reply
   `Claim recorded for @<login> - label and assignee set (only collaborators can set labels; your comment is the claim).`
-  A contributor's claim does not go stale on a timer; it stands while the
-  comment exists.
 
 **Withdraw.** For every open issue carrying `claimed`
 (`gh issue list --state open --label claimed --limit 200`), look for the
 claim behind it: a claim comment by a non-owner (or an agent's `claimed:`
 comment, which follows the 4 h rule instead). If the only claim behind the
 label was a contributor's comment that is now deleted, or that contributor
-later commented `unclaim`, remove the label and their assignment
+later withdrew it (`unclaim`, `/unclaim`, "claim withdrawn", "releasing
+this claim", "the issue is free" in their last comment), remove the label
+and their assignment
 (`gh issue edit N --remove-label claimed --remove-assignee <login>`) and
-comment `claim by @<login> withdrawn (comment removed) - issue is free again`.
+comment `claim by @<login> withdrawn - issue is free again`.
+If the claim is neither withdrawn nor released but is **stale** (none of:
+an open PR for the issue, a commit on the claimant's branch in the last
+48 hours, a comment by the claimant on the issue in the last 48 hours),
+remove the label and assignment the same way and comment
+`claim by @<login> released (stale: no open PR, branch commit or comment from the claimant for 48 h) - issue is free again; claim it again with a new comment if you are working on it`.
+An issue that carries a "released by the maintainer" or "released
+(stale ...)" comment after its claim comment is free: never mirror that
+old claim again. Never change the labels of a `P?` issue in this pass,
+stale claim or not - list it in the report for the maintainer instead.
 A label with no findable claim of any kind and no "Claim recorded" reply
 was set by a collaborator by hand: leave it.

     issue's comments (`gh issue view N --comments`). A claim comment by
     anyone other than the owner account (agents post as the owner) means
     the issue is taken: do not work it, even if it has no `claimed` label -

-  - **Mirror it.** An issue found with such a comment but without the
+    unless the claim is withdrawn, released or stale (below).
+  - **Mirror it.** An issue with a live claim comment (next point) but no
     label gets `claimed` and the claimant as assignee (if GitHub refuses
     the assignee, the label alone), plus one reply: "Claim recorded for
     @<login> - label and assignee set (only collaborators can set labels;
-    your comment is the claim)."
-  - **Withdrawn = deleted.** A contributor's claim stands for as long as
-    their claim comment exists - the 4 h stale rule is for agent claims

+    your comment is the claim)." Only a LIVE earlier claim by someone else
+    holds an issue against a new claimant; a stale or ended one does not.
+    When a new claimant comes over a stale earlier claim, release the
+    stale one first (its release comment ends it, next point), then mirror
+    the new claim: the label and the assignee always follow the newest
+    live claim.
+  - **A claim must be live - an old one cannot stall an issue** (user,
+    2026-11-11, on eight issues a contributor's agents had claimed days
+    earlier and left: "unclaim those 8 old ones and let someone pick em up
+    and fix em they can't stall"). A contributor's claim is live while at
+    least one of these holds: an open PR by the claimant for the issue; a
+    commit on the claimant's branch for it in the last 48 hours; or a
+    comment by the claimant on the issue in the last 48 hours (the claim
+    itself, progress, findings - any comment of theirs counts; the rule is
+    kept simple on purpose). Research claims have no branch, so the
+    comment is what keeps them live. With none of the three, the claim is
+    **stale**: do not mirror it; if it carries `claimed`, remove the label
+    and the assignment and comment "claim by @<login> released (stale: no
+    open PR, branch commit or comment from the claimant for 48 h) - issue
+    is free again; claim it again with a new comment if you are working on
+    it". That comment ENDS the claim (next point): a later comment by the
+    claimant does not revive it, only a new claim line does. Ended beats
+    live: a comment that withdraws or releases a claim is not activity
+    that keeps it live, and an ended claim is never live again. The 4 h rule
+    above stays the rule for the owner account's own agents. A `P?` issue
+    is never relabelled by an agent, stale claim or not: report it to the
+    maintainer instead.
+  - **Withdrawn or released.** A claim also ends when its comment is
+    deleted; when the claimant's later comment withdraws it (`unclaim`,
+    `/unclaim`, "claim withdrawn", "releasing this claim", "the issue is
+    free" - read the claimant's LAST comment, not only the claim line);
+    when the maintainer releases it (a comment saying the claim is
+    released by the maintainer); or when an agent has released it as stale
+    (the comment above). Then: remove `claimed` and their assignment, and
+    comment "claim by @<login> withdrawn - issue is free again" (not needed
+    where a release comment already says so). Only a NEW `claimed:` /
+    `/claim` comment posted after that is a claim again; an ended claim is
+    never mirrored back from its old comment.

-    claims, and drop the label where the only claim comment behind it is

-    4 h rule above instead.
+    does this sweep for the issues it touches: label the live
+    comment-only claims, and drop the label where the claim behind it is
+    withdrawn, released or stale. A `claimed` label backed by one of the
